newsitem.title: USA: Clinton praises embattled labor nominee Herman.
newsitem.headline: Clinton praises embattled labor nominee Herman.

text.p: President Clinton on Monday praised Alexis Herman, his embattled nominee to run the Labour Department, saying she would make a "great" labour secretary.

At a White House meeting with presidents of black colleges and universities, Clinton singled out Herman, saying she "did a superb job for us as director of public liaison (and) with your help will be a great secretary of labour."
Herman's nomination has become bogged down in the Senate, where the labour and human resources committee has yet to schedule a vote on her candidacy.

Labour Committee Chairman Jim Jeffords, a Vermont Republican, issued a statement Monday afternoon saying Herman's confirmation hearing was likely to take place in March. But he said the date would depend on when the White House responded to questions about the nominee.

"The hearing will take place approximately two weeks after receipt of complete answers to questions now pending before the administration, barring additional revelations from the White House that would have a bearing on the nomination," Jeffords said.

Senate Republicans have questioned whether Herman may have violated the law when her White House office invited a federal banking regulator, Comptroller of the Currency Eugene Ludwig, to a White House political coffee meeting with Clinton and bankers.

Clinton has said it was a mistake for Ludwig to attend and Herman has said she decided not to go to the meeting when she found out Democratic National Committee officials would be there. As the White House director of public liason, Herman was responsible for reaching out to interest groups.
The White House, and Clinton himself, have consistently said she would make a good labour secretary and called for the Senate to schedule a vote.
On Friday, White House Chief of Staff Erskine Bowles met with 75 representatives from labour, women's and civil rights groups to urge them to come to her defence.
